reason: The hypothesis integrates three distinct techniques—high-rate laser calorimetry, in-situ acoustic emission, and machine-learning-refined CALPHAD—into a single method for simultaneous determination of multiple melting parameters, a combination not proposed or demonstrated in any passage. It also introduces acoustic emission to resolve two-stage melting and volumetric changes, directly addressing a conflict between MD simulations (P1) and conventional DSC, which is a novel synthesis beyond the literature.
